messages:
joni: After the auto-upgrade yesterday my zsh startup got really slow. Noticed the installer appended a call to `eval \"$(redwoodctl completion zsh)\"` into my ~/.zshrc and it seems to block for ~2s on each new shell. On macOS Big Sur with zinit it makes every new tab feel laggy.

tasha: Oof. We used to append completions so users get them out of the box, but 2s is too long. Can you run `time redwoodctl completion zsh` and paste output?

joni: `redwoodctl completion zsh` is itself fast (<50ms) when run interactively, but the eval in rc runs `redwoodctl --config /Users/joni/.redwood/rc completion zsh` in a noninteractive shell and ends up sourcing network-config checks and the telemetry init which adds delay. Repro: open new terminal -> observe `zsh: no job control` flicker then prompt delayed.

raul: That sounds like our installer wrote a heavy completion wrapper instead of the static completion stub. We should ship a static completion script that calls `redwoodctl completion zsh --static` so it doesn't do runtime checks. Two choices: 1) change installer to write static stub, 2) add lazy-loading snippet that runs `redwoodctl completion` only when the `redwoodctl` command is invoked.

joni: Lazy-loading would be best for our setup. Example lazy snippet that fixed it for me:```
# lazy load redwoodctl completions
_redwood_lazy(){
  autoload -Uz compinit && compinit
  eval \"$(redwoodctl completion zsh --static)\"
  unfunction _redwood_lazy
}
compdef _redwood_lazy redwoodctl
```

tasha: Nice. We'll update the installer. Also tagging the auth folks: while debugging I hit another issue in our CI where `redwoodctl auth login` is used in headless docker and the CLI attempted to open a browser and then failed the job. We should make `redwoodctl login` error more clearly when no display is present and prefer device or headless flows automatically in CI environments.

raul: Agree. We already have `REDWOOD_AUTH_FLOW=device` env var but it's not documented widely. Proposal: 1) detect CI (CI env vars) or no `xdg-open`/`open`/`start` and fall back to device flow with a clear log message; 2) return distinct exit codes for interactive vs headless login (so CI can fail fast if misconfigured).

joni: For now I added `ENV REDWOOD_AUTH_FLOW=device` to our Dockerfile and switched the installer to not inject completion into noninteractive shells. That fixed both the startup lag and CI flakiness.

devex-bot: Filed DEVEX-7893 (installer: use static or lazy zsh completions; detect noninteractive shells) and ENG-8001 (auth: auto-fallback to device flow in CI and expose exit codes).
